text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government to build one million new flats at a total cost of 35.8 billion pounds ($10.5 billion) within the next five years. State will continue to provide housing loans and will study a proposal to increase their value by five percent a year to counteract higher prices.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak to deliver a speech to mark Police Day.
- Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid says state has deposited in the Central Bank 1.595 billion pounds of its net yield from privatising state firms in the past six months.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa to go to Saudi Arabia to deliver a message from Mubarak to King Fahd.
- Mubarak speaks today to mark Police Day. Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi says the president is following the security situation and is concerned about the security of new communities.
- Mubarak to inaugurate the new police academy and distribute medals to distinguished officers and the families of police martyrs.
- State security arrests members of Moslem militant Jihad group before they execute a terrorist plot.
- Spain's king to visit Cairo on February 18.
- Court throws out lawyer's case calling for the state to stop publication of crime tabloid "Akhbar al-Hawadith".
- State to spend one billion pounds to restructure flagging public sector companies. Obeid: wages to increase and state to set up companies for technical restructuring.
- Finance Minister Mohiedeen el-Gharib says prices of goods to fall by the end of this month.
- Devil worshippers tell the prosecutor: Michael Jackson is our idol, and blood and drugs are our life.
